faq.a: AOD-9604 is classified as a gh fragment. Its mechanism of action involves: synthetic fragment of the C-terminal lipolytic region of GH. In rodent studies it stimulated lipolysis and inhibited lipogenesis in adipose tissue without binding the GH receptor or altering IGF-1; beta-3 adrenergic receptor involvement was examined but did not fully account for the effect (PMID 11713213).

In laboratory and preclinical settings, AOD-9604 is researched for its potential effects on lipolysis in adipose tissue (rodent models), body-weight endpoints in phase ii obesity trials, cartilage repair (rabbit osteoarthritis model). It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.
No, AOD-9604 is not FDA-approved. It is classified exclusively as a research compound and is legally available solely for in-vitro and laboratory experimentation, not for human or animal consumption.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, Kisspeptin-10 is researched for its potential effects on lh and testosterone secretion in small human studies, lh pulsatility in hypogonadal men (small trial), oocyte-maturation trigger in ivf research (kisspeptin-54), hpg axis signaling. faq.a: LL-37 is classified as a antimicrobial peptide. Its mechanism of action involves: the only human cathelicidin antimicrobial peptide. LL-37 is a 37-amino acid cationic peptide that directly disrupts microbial membranes (bacteria, viruses, fungi) and neutralizes bacterial endotoxins (LPS). Beyond direct antimicrobial action, LL-37 modulates innate immunity by chemoattracting neutrophils, monocytes, and T-cells to infection sites. In wound models it stimulated keratinocyte migration via EGFR transactivation, and in vitro it inhibited Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm formation at sub-MIC concentrations.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, LL-37 is researched for its potential effects on antimicrobial membrane disruption (in vitro), biofilm inhibition (in vitro), keratinocyte migration and re-epithelialization (cell and wound models), innate immune modulation. In laboratory and preclinical settings, ARA-290 is researched for its potential effects on small-fiber neuropathy symptoms (small phase 2 trials), corneal nerve fiber density (small trials), innate repair receptor signaling. faq.a: Gonadorelin is classified as a gnrh analog. Its mechanism of action involves: synthetic decapeptide identical to endogenous gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH). Binds GnRH receptors in the anterior pituitary, stimulating pulsatile release of luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH). It appears in some compounded protocols alongside testosterone therapy, but that use has not been evaluated in the controlled trials cited here. Physiologic GnRH signaling is pulsatile — continuous exposure causes receptor downregulation.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, Gonadorelin is researched for its potential effects on pituitary lh/fsh release (gnrh receptor agonist), pulsatile gnrh in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (clinical studies), hpg axis diagnostic testing (formerly fda-approved as factrel). It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.
Yes, Gonadorelin is FDA-approved for specific clinical indications. Research-grade material is intended strictly for laboratory use and is not approved for human medical use.

faq.a: Larazotide is classified as a zonulin antagonist. Its mechanism of action involves: synthetic octapeptide developed as a tight-junction regulator. Zonulin, which can be released in response to gliadin, is a regulator of intestinal tight-junction permeability, and larazotide was designed as a zonulin antagonist. In epithelial cell studies it reduced gliadin-induced tight-junction disruption and permeability (one study describes a zonulin-independent mechanism). It acts locally in the gut lumen with minimal systemic absorption.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, Larazotide is researched for its potential effects on tight-junction regulation (epithelial cell studies), tested in celiac disease trials (phase 2b/3, adjunct to gluten-free diet), gliadin-induced intestinal permeability. It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.

No, Larazotide is not FDA-approved. It is classified exclusively as a research compound and is legally available solely for in-vitro and laboratory experimentation, not for human or animal consumption.

faq.a: VIP is classified as a neuropeptide. Its mechanism of action involves: 28-amino acid neuropeptide that binds VPAC1 and VPAC2 receptors, activating cAMP pathways to produce broad anti-inflammatory effects. Inhibits TNF-alpha, IL-6, and IL-12 production while promoting Th2/Treg tolerance. Pulmonary vasodilator and bronchodilator. It is used in some clinician-directed protocols for chronic inflammatory response syndrome (CIRS); evidence for that use is limited to small uncontrolled series.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, VIP is researched for its potential effects on anti-inflammatory signaling in macrophages (cell studies), vasodilatory and bronchodilatory effects, cirs (small uncontrolled case series). It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.
No, VIP is not FDA-approved. It is classified exclusively as a research compound and is legally available solely for in-vitro and laboratory experimentation, not for human or animal consumption.

faq.a: Oxytocin is classified as a neuropeptide. Its mechanism of action involves: nonapeptide produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary. Binds oxytocin receptors (OXTR) broadly expressed in brain, heart, gut, and immune cells. Studied for modulation of the HPA-axis stress response, social behavior, and GI motility. Intranasal administration is used in research to study central effects.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, Oxytocin is researched for its potential effects on cortisol and anxiety response to social stress (human rct), social cognition, gastric motility (clinical research), fda-approved obstetric uses (iv/im form). It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.

faq.a: Thymalin is classified as a thymic peptide. Its mechanism of action involves: polypeptide extract from animal thymus gland containing a mixture of thymic hormones including thymulin, thymosin, and thymopoietin. Reported in Russian studies to promote T-cell differentiation and to modulate the balance between Th1/Th2 responses. Khavinson-group publications describe effects on neuroendocrine and immune markers in aging; independent replication is limited.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, Thymalin is researched for its potential effects on immune markers in elderly patients (russian cohort studies), long-term mortality in an elderly cohort (with epithalamin), t-cell differentiation. faq.a: Humanin is classified as a mitochondrial peptide. Its mechanism of action involves: 21-amino acid mitochondrial-derived peptide (MOTS-c sibling peptide) encoded in the 16S rRNA gene of mitochondrial DNA. Binds formyl peptide receptor-like 1 (FPRL1/FPR2) and the gp130 co-receptor complex, activating STAT3 and PI3K/Akt survival signaling. In cell and rodent studies it inhibited Bax-mediated apoptosis, reduced amyloid-beta neurotoxicity, and improved insulin sensitivity. Circulating levels decline with age.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, Humanin is researched for its potential effects on neuroprotection against amyloid-beta toxicity (cell models), insulin sensitivity (rodent models), anti-apoptotic signaling. It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.

faq.a: PE-22-28 is classified as a nootropic peptide. Its mechanism of action involves: synthetic peptide derived from spadin, a fragment of the sortilin propeptide that regulates the TREK-1 potassium channel. PE-22-28 inhibits TREK-1, a background potassium channel implicated in rodent models of depression. In rodent studies, TREK-1 inhibition by spadin and its analogs increased hippocampal BDNF expression and produced antidepressant-like effects in behavioral tests.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, PE-22-28 is researched for its potential effects on trek-1 inhibition studied in rodent depression models, hippocampal bdnf expression (rodent models), neuroplasticity. It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.

faq.a: Dihexa is classified as a neurotropic peptide. Its mechanism of action involves: angiotensin IV analog developed at Washington State University. Binds hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) and potentiates its binding to the c-Met receptor, which in rodent studies was associated with increased dendritic spine density in hippocampal neurons. faq.a: FOXO4-DRI is classified as a senolytic peptide. Its mechanism of action involves: d-retro-inverso peptide that disrupts the interaction between FOXO4 and p53 in senescent cells. In normal cells, FOXO4 retains p53 in the nucleus preventing apoptosis — a mechanism senescent cells exploit for survival. FOXO4-DRI competitively binds FOXO4, freeing p53 to migrate to mitochondria, triggering apoptosis selectively in senescent cells. In aged and chemotherapy-treated mice, this was associated with reduced senescent-cell burden and improved fur density, fitness, and renal function.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, FOXO4-DRI is researched for its potential effects on selective apoptosis of senescent cells (mouse models), fur density, fitness and renal function in aged mice, senolytic research tool. It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.

faq.a: Klotho is classified as a anti-aging protein. Its mechanism of action involves: klotho is a type-I transmembrane aging-suppressor protein expressed primarily in kidney tubular cells and brain choroid plexus. Cleaved extracellularly to generate soluble Klotho, which circulates systemically and acts as a co-receptor for FGF23, regulating phosphate and vitamin D metabolism. Also directly inhibits IGF-1 and Wnt signaling pathways that drive cellular senescence. Circulating Klotho declines with age. In one study, a single systemic administration of soluble Klotho enhanced cognitive performance in aged mice and nonhuman primates.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, Klotho is researched for its potential effects on cognitive performance in aged mice and nonhuman primates (single-administration study), fgf23 co-receptor and phosphate regulation, low serum levels associated with cognitive decline (human cohort). It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.

faq.a: Synapsin is classified as a nootropic peptide. Its mechanism of action involves: compounded intranasal formulation (not a single peptide) combining Rg3 (ginsenoside), NAD+, and additional compounds. In preclinical models, Rg3 modulated NMDA receptor activity, inhibited NF-kB-mediated neuroinflammation, and increased BDNF expression. NAD+ is a cofactor in mitochondrial metabolism and sirtuin activity. Intranasal delivery is proposed to bypass the blood-brain barrier. The blend itself has not been evaluated in clinical trials.

In laboratory and preclinical settings, Synapsin is researched for its potential effects on neuroprotective effects of the ginsenoside rg3 component (preclinical models), nf-kb and bdnf signaling (rg3, preclinical), compounded intranasal formulation (rg3 + nad+). faq.a: FGL Loop is classified as a neurotropic peptide. Its mechanism of action involves: synthetic peptide derived from the fibronectin type III (F3) module of Neural Cell Adhesion Molecule (NCAM). Mimics the homophilic binding of NCAM, activating FGFR (fibroblast growth factor receptor) signaling downstream. In hippocampal slices and rodent models it enhanced long-term potentiation (LTP) and spatial learning; reviews also describe neuroprotective effects in animal models of aging.

faq.a: In laboratory and preclinical settings, FGL Loop is researched for its potential effects on long-term potentiation and spatial learning (rodent models), ncam-mimetic fgfr signaling, neuroprotection in animal models of aging. It is strictly for experimental study and not intended for human consumption.
No, FGL Loop is not FDA-approved. It is classified exclusively as a research compound and is legally available solely for in-vitro and laboratory experimentation, not for human or animal consumption.
